definition: Merging multiple GPU operations into one kernel so intermediate results stay in fast on-chip memory instead of round-tripping to HBM.
details: Merging multiple GPU operations into one kernel so intermediate results stay in fast on-chip memory instead of round-tripping to HBM. The single most important principle of GPU performance work, and the core trick behind FlashAttention's speedup.

explainer.lead: Kernel fusion merges multiple GPU operations into one kernel so intermediate results stay in fast on-chip memory instead of round-tripping to HBM. It is described as the single most important principle of GPU performance work and the core trick behind FlashAttention's speedup.

tiers.eli5: Instead of running to the fridge for every ingredient, you keep everything on the counter and cook in one go.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fuse elementwise and reduction steps to cut memory traffic; a pitfall is that fusing too much can increase register pressure and reduce occupancy.
tiers.paperLevel: Combining several GPU operations into a single kernel so intermediates remain in on-chip memory rather than being written to and read back from HBM.

explainer.example: Merging an add, a multiply and a reduction into one kernel avoids writing the intermediate tensor to HBM between steps.
